--- CRITICAL FINDINGS ---

[DB-1] Production creates new DB clients per import
File: src/lib/db.ts (L1-L40)
Evidence: The code only caches PrismaClient on globalThis when NODE_ENV !== "production", so in production each module load creates new PrismaClient instances (new DB connections) instead of a singleton. This pattern exhausts database connections in serverless/ephemeral environments.
Impact: Connection pool exhaustion and refused connections under modest concurrent traffic (~50–200 concurrent requests depending on DB plan), causing errors and severe latency spikes.
Fix: Always reuse a singleton PrismaClient (store on globalThis in all environments) or route connections through a dedicated pooler (PgBouncer / connection pool) and configure pool limits.

[DB-2] Hot-row writes: chat messages stored as ever-growing JSON arrays
File: actions/chat.ts (L1-L220)
Evidence: addMessageToChat/getProjectChat read the entire projectChat/chat row (messages: Json[]) then append and update the whole messages array; messages are unbounded and rewritten on every message add. No append-only table, pagination, or partial update is used.
Impact: With frequent messaging, single-row hot locks, large row writes, high DB IOPS and lock contention will occur (data loss/race conditions and throughput collapse under 10x QPS on active chats).
Fix: Model messages as append-only rows in a dedicated messages table (one INSERT per message), or store paginated shards and perform atomic appends/streaming writes instead of rewriting a large JSON array.

[DB-1] Production creates new DB clients per import
File: src/lib/db.ts (L1-L40)
Evidence: The code only caches PrismaClient on globalThis when NODE_ENV !== "production", so in production each module load creates new PrismaClient instances (new DB connections) instead of a singleton. This pattern exhausts database connections in serverless/ephemeral environments.
Impact: Connection pool exhaustion and refused connections under modest concurrent traffic (~50–200 concurrent requests depending on DB plan), causing errors and severe latency spikes.
Fix: Always reuse a singleton PrismaClient (store on globalThis in all environments) or route connections through a dedicated pooler (PgBouncer / connection pool) and configure pool limits.

[DB-2] Hot-row writes: chat messages stored as ever-growing JSON arrays
File: actions/chat.ts (L1-L220)
Evidence: addMessageToChat/getProjectChat read the entire projectChat/chat row (messages: Json[]) then append and update the whole messages array; messages are unbounded and rewritten on every message add. No append-only table, pagination, or partial update is used.
Impact: With frequent messaging, single-row hot locks, large row writes, high DB IOPS and lock contention will occur (data loss/race conditions and throughput collapse under 10x QPS on active chats).
Fix: Model messages as append-only rows in a dedicated messages table (one INSERT per message), or store paginated shards and perform atomic appends/streaming writes instead of rewriting a large JSON array.

[DB-3] Webhook subscription flow lacks transactional safety (financial)
File: src/app/api/webhook/dodo/route.ts (L1-L140) and src/lib/subscription-helpers.ts (L1-L220)
Evidence: Webhook handler invokes SubscriptionService methods that perform upserts and follow-up user updates in separate queries (read-then-write sequences) with no db.$transaction or idempotent guard; failures leave partial state (subscription vs user credits) inconsistent.
Impact: Partial application of billing events will cause financial inconsistency (wrong plan/credits) and require manual reconciliation; at scale intermittent failures will cause a high rate of inconsistent accounts.
Fix: Wrap subscription upsert + related user updates in a single transaction and add webhook idempotency checking (use WebhookEvent dedupe table or db-level unique key + transaction).

--- WARNING FINDINGS ---

[DB-4] Missing index on Project.userId (table scans)
File: actions/project.ts (getProjects) (L1-L40) and prisma/schema.prisma (Project model) (L1-L80)
Evidence: getProjects runs db.project.findMany({ where: { userId } }) but the Project model has no index on userId in schema.prisma, forcing full-table scans as Project rows grow.
Impact: Read latency and DB CPU/IOPS degrade once Projects → 100k+ rows, causing slow responses for per-user project lists under higher QPS.
Fix: Add an index on Project.userId (@@index([userId])) and deploy a migration; consider including createdAt for common order patterns.

[DB-5] Unbounded relation fetch (user → chats) returns full histories
File: actions/user.ts (getUserById) (L1-L80)
Evidence: getUserById includes chats without take/limit, returning the entire chat set (and potentially large message payloads) in one query.
Impact: Large payloads and heavy reads for users with many chats will increase latency and memory usage, causing slow pages or timeouts as traffic grows.
Fix: Limit included relations (take with orderBy or use cursor pagination) and fetch messages/pages on demand.

--- INFO ---

[DB-6] PostgreSQL + Prisma used; dev singleton present
File: prisma/schema.prisma and src/lib/db.ts
Evidence: prisma/schema.prisma declares provider = "postgresql" and db.ts implements a singleton only for non-production environments.
